newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FOREST RELEGATED ON DAY OF HIGH DRAMA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FOREST RELEGATED ON DAY OF HIGH DRAMA.

text.p: Nottingham Forest were relegated from the English premier league on Saturday after drawing 1-1 at home with Wimbledon -- but Manchester United's title celebrations were put on hold after they could only draw 2-2 at Leicester.
Elsewhere a last-minute penalty gave Middlesbrough a 3-2 victory over Aston Villa while West Ham, Sunderland and Southampton also won as the relegation battle goes to the wire.

Arsenal lost 1-0 at home to Newcastle putting Arsenal out of the title race, but Newcastle could yet pip Manchester United if they win their last three games and United get less than three points from their last three matches.
Liverpool, who were playing Tottenham later on Saturtday were also still mathematically in the hunt.
Depending on that result, United can still win the title in front of their own fans by beating Middlesbrough at Old Trafford on Monday.

That would leave all attention focused on relegation issues with everything being settled next Sunday -- and if the drama reaches Saturday's levels, there will be plenty of anxious moments for fans and players alike.
Forest returned to the first division three seasons after coming up as other results made their City Ground point too little too late.
Oyvind Leonhardson put Wimbledon ahead early with Brian Roy equalising in the 56th minute.
General manager Dave Bassett, who is something of an expert in keeping teams up against the odds, arrived at the club too late to turn things round.
He is likely to take over team selection duties from Stuart Pearce, and said: "It's a horrible feeling being relegated -- but you can bounce back."
Middlesbrough looked doomed to join Forest after blowing a 2-0 lead at home to Aston Villa -- only for Fabrizio Ravanelli to secure a lifeline with his spot kick in injury time.
The Italian and Mikkel Beck had Boro 2-0 up after 20 minutes only for Ugo Ehiogu and Savo Milosevic to level things in the second half.
Then Gareth Farrelly fouled Craig Hignett and Ravanelli kept his cool to score -- his 31st goal in Boro's incredible roller coaster season.
West Ham produced a fantastic performance to thrash Sheffield Wednesday 5-1, with a hat-trick for Paul Kitson and two for John Hartson.
The Hammers were 3-0 up after 30 minutes and are now one of four teams on 41 points.
Boro have 36 but have three games to play while Coventry have 38 and Sunderland 40 -- both with one game left.
Sunderland said farewell to Roker Park, their home for 99 years, with a 3-0 victory over Everton that drags the Merseysiders back into the relegation equation.
Paul Stewart, Chris Waddle and Allan Johnston were the scorers.

Southampton's good form continued with a 2-0 home win over Blackburn, who are also under threat. Robbie Slater in the 22nd and substitute Mathew Le Tissier were on target while Blackburn skipper Tim Sherwood was sent off for spitting in the face of Jim Magilton.

Coventry once again face a last day scramble for safety after losing 2-1 at home to Derby. Gary Rowett put Derby ahead in the 49th, Gary McAllister equalised from the penalty spot 10 minutes later but Dean Sturridge secured the points for Derby in the 67th minute.
Newcastle kept in contention for at least the runners-up spot thanks to Robbie Elliot's 44th minute header at Highbury.
Arsenal stay second on 65 points, five behind United. Liverpool are third on 64 with Newcastle fourth on 63.
In a morning kick off Manchester United had to come from 2-0 down to draw at Leicester.
Steve Walsh and Ian Marshall had the home side deservedly in front early on but Ole Gunnar Solskjaer scored either side of half time to keep United on course for their fourth title in five years.
"I am very happy with a draw," said United manager Alex Ferguson. "The international week took a lot out of our players."
"Now it would be great to win it in front of our own fans."

Chelsea and Leeds drew 0-0 in the day's other game while Hereford were relegated from the Football League after drawing 1-1 at home with Brighton. They will be replaced by Conference champions Macclesfield, managed by Sammy McIlroy the former Manchester United and Northern Ireland international.
